Small state park on Mississippi River backwater channels.  Several sites are right on the water with direct river access.  --AWH
The electric sites are all in the north campground. The south campground's waterfront sites have none, their shore is lined with large erosion rocks, and that campground stays closed in Mississippi flood years until the water recedes. --Claude

flags: WATERFRONT --AWH 'riverfront' (report only): agrees. DNR: South campground '35 campsites, including 28 waterfront sites on Fountain City Bay'; property page 'some sites in the south campground have river access for mooring watercraft or fishing directly from the sites'. Imagery: the South campground runs ~1.3 km SE from the boat landing (44.1500,-91.7496) along a narrow peninsula, its pads at the shoreline (~10-20 m) of a channel 100 m+ wide, under scattered trees; site numbers 51-87 per the DNR map (exact waterfront numbers not stated). Shoreline is armoured with large rocks ('set along the shore to halt erosion and protect campsites') - a riprap caveat by the 2026-11-12 rule. The North loop (25 sites, the electric ones) is 70-100 m from backwater through dense forest: not waterfront on its own.

PIN: stored 44.1504,-91.7518 is in woods by the island/boat-landing area, ~0.7 km from the South campground centre and ~1.4 km from the North loop. Proposed: the South campground centre ~44.1466,-91.7448 (waterfront sites, 35 of the 60 drive-in sites); the North loop (electric) is at ~44.1597,-91.7622. Not a split proposal: one DNR park with one contact station at the park entrance, but the two drive-in campgrounds are ~1.8 km apart.
